text:
ConocoPhillips rose modestly today as oil prices climbed further on geopolitical tension. Brent crude hit its highest level since May at over $113 a barrel following reports that the U.S. is preparing military action against Iran and has withdrawn diplomats from Saudi Arabia—moves that raise the risk of fresh Middle East conflict and potential supply disruptions. For an integrated oil company like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost the value of reserves and profits on production.

The broader energy trade has been moving upward for two weeks, driven by these same regional risks. Ukraine's ongoing drone strikes on Russian refineries have also tightened diesel supplies globally, adding to the bullish pressure on energy stocks. With midterm elections two weeks away and political attention on energy prices, the market is pricing in continued volatility and the possibility of further supply shocks.
